In April 1915 Britain, France and Russia made Italy a secret offer: join our side and take a big piece of the Adriatic. The broken promise would haunt Italy for decades.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The Treaty of London was signed on 26 April 1915. Italy was still formally allied with Germany and Austria-Hungary but had stayed neutral. The Entente wanted it in the war to draw Austrian troops away from other fronts.

2/ The price: Trentino and South Tyrol, Trieste and Istria, and northern Dalmatia with Zadar and Šibenik plus many islands. That's the green on this map. The rest of the coast was left for Croatia, Serbia and Montenegro.
3/ Italy was also promised Vlorë in Albania, the Dodecanese and more colonies. The Adriatic gains alone would have brought around 600,000 South Slavs and 200,000 German speakers under Italian rule.
4/ Serbia's consolation was Bosnia and an Adriatic outlet, while the Entente dangled Macedonian land in front of Bulgaria. Serbian leader Pašić protested that Serbia hadn't even been consulted.

5/ Italy declared war on Austria-Hungary in May 1915, but waited a year before declaring war on Germany. The treaty's full text only became public after the October Revolution, when the Bolsheviks published it.
6/ At Paris in 1919 the US pushed to void the deal. Italy got South Tyrol and the Julian March, but not Dalmatia. Talk of a "mutilated victory" followed, and D'Annunzio led veterans to seize Fiume.
Did Italy get cheated in 1919, or did it ask for too much in 1915? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
